sentences.text:
---- Applicant
 Versus
  State Of Chhattisgarh, Through P.S. Kotwali, District Raigarh,
 Chhattisgarh.

---- Respondent
For Applicant : Mr. Devershi Thakur, Advocate.

For Objector : Ms. Gunjan Tiwari along with
Sandeep Jha, and Dr. Sachin Ashok Kale, counsels for the respective objectors.

For State/Respondent : Mr. Avinash K. Mishra, G.A. Hon'ble Justice Smt. Rajani Dubey Order on
Board 20.01.2023
1.

The applicant has preferred this first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., as he is
apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.1363/2022, registered at Police Station
Kotwali, District Raigarh (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 120b of Ipc & under
Sections 04, 05 & 06 of C.G.P.I.D Act, 2005.

2.  The prosecution story in brief is that the present applicant being a manager/agent of the Sahara India Company allured the complainants to invest huge amount of money in the said company, but upon their investment of huge amount, the said company has been banned by SEBI and their money has not been returned to them.
Thereafter, a case was got registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present crime in question.

This Court has granted anticipatory bail to the similarly placed co-accused personspassed in MCRCA No.1177/2019 (Mulchand Dewangan & Others Vs. State of Chhattisgarh & Another) vide order dated 19.09.2019, MCRCA No.643/2017 (Vinod Kumar Vs.
State of Chhattisgarh) vide order dated 10.11.2017 and also passed order in MCRCA No.174/2018 Amrit Shriwas vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642238/
1 (Mahendra Sahu Vs. State of Chhattisgarh) vide order dated 26.04.2018.

sentences.text: He further submits that the applicant was only the manager of the company and was nowhere involved in the commission of the present crime in question.
He further submits that the State Government is already withdrawing the cases against the agents and managers of financial companies.

He next submits that as per the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the matter of "(MAD) - 2015 - 6 - 58, Ulagananthan vs State of Tamilnadu", an agent cannot be fastened with liability to repay the funds invested with the companies.
Therefore, the present bail application is maintainable and thus, the applicant may kindly be released on anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for State vehemently opposes the bail application and submits that this bail application is not maintainable.

He further submits that applicant is a manager of the company and he collected the money from the complainants so he is responsible for the criminal act and investigation is in primary stage so this bail application is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed.

5. Learned counsel for the objector strongly opposes the bail application and submits that the applicant is a sector manager of the society run by the Sahara India and convinced the objectors and motivated them to invested such a big amount in the society.
They further submits that the accused with a prior criminal intention cheated the objectors and others as well and presently the offence is in preliminary stage.
Therefore, under these circumstances, the applicant may not be released on anticipatory bail.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary carefully.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly the fact that huge amount is involved in the present case and the applicant is a manager of the concerned company and he is in a position to affect the investigation and the investigation is also at preliminary stage, I am not inclined to release him on anticipatory bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail is rejected.

Sd/-
